## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

The *Seyyajātaka* (Ja 310) is a narrative belonging to the canonical Pali *Jātaka* collection. According to the traditional nidāna recorded in its opening blurb, the Buddha recounted this past-life story while residing at the Jetavana monastery outside Sāvatthī. The tale was occasioned by a backsliding bhikkhu who, while walking on his alms round in the city, caught sight of a beautiful woman and subsequently grew discontented, abandoning his joy in the Dhamma. The text is also explicitly referenced in the post-canonical *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.5.5, *Buddhaaviheṭhakapañha*).

  The secondary literature passages in the present dossier do not provide direct analysis of Ja 310, referring instead to the homonymous *Seyyajātaka* (Ja 282) or addressing unrelated grammatical and Vinaya occurrences of the Pali term *seyyā*.
